decision: routed to figure-it-out, not Feature
why: greenfield multi-part build with a data pipeline, a renderer and a print path; the audit trail is the point

decision: fired two recon agents before designing anything
why: the ICGC data formats and MapLibre texture-fill limits are the two facts the whole architecture hangs on

decision: pulled the real OSM data first, before any design
why: wanted the actual feature mix, not my guess at it: 48 dive spots, 343 mooring buoys, 3 wrecks, 33 restricted areas

decision: found the textures: Crosshead Dungeondraft packs, 2048px not 1024
why: user pointed at ~/Pictures; the pack ships .dungeondraft_tags, so these are VTT map assets

decision: wrote a seam checker instead of eyeballing the textures
why: a seam invisible on screen is obvious on a laminated A3 print; needed a number

decision: user chose: all Catalonia, annotations in git, SvelteKit, strictest TS
why: answers to the framing questions

decision: MapLibre GL 6.9, not Leaflet or OpenLayers
why: it is the only one with a built-in hillshade over a custom DEM; OpenLayers would mean hand-writing the slope maths
evidence: recon agent ran it in a real browser

decision: downscale the 2048px Crosshead textures to 512 at pixelRatio 2
why: 1024 works but MapLibre packs the pattern atlas per tile, so 30 visible tiles cost ~126MB of GPU texture
evidence: measured in maplibre-gl 6.9.0 source and a live page

decision: fill-pattern grain is fixed in screen pixels, not on the ground
why: found by reading webgl/program/pattern.ts; no style option changes it
result: ACCEPTED, matches how paper chart hatching works

decision: add a color-relief layer for the depth tint, on top of hillshade
why: shade alone does not tell you which way is down; the hypsometric ramp does
evidence: maplibre-gl 5.6.0+ color-relief-color takes an elevation expression

decision: bake contours at 1m with gdal_contour, filter the interval in the style
why: drops the maplibre-contour dependency, whose npm latest is 0.1.0 from 2024 while its repo moved on

decision: print export needs maxCanvasSize [8192,8192]
why: the 4096 default silently downscales A3/300dpi to 2893x4096 and getPixelRatio still lies about it

decision: terra-draw 1.33 for annotations, not mapbox-gl-draw
why: mapbox-gl-draw hardcodes mapboxgl-* CSS classes so the toolbar goes dead under MapLibre

decision: isobaths already exist as 1m vectors, dropping the gdal_contour plan
why: ICGC publishes batimetria_5000.fgb, spatially indexed FlatGeobuf, range-readable, with ready-made generalisation tiers

decision: DEM for the hillshade is a 3.33GB COG, clip by range request
why: 1m float32 EPSG:25831; downloading all of it to render Catalonia is not worth 3.3GB

decision: habitats come from the gencat WFS, not a download page
why: there is no download page; the project viewer's own button is a GetFeature call

decision: 33 habitat classes and 20 substrate classes drive the texture palette
why: transcribed from the v1r0 specs; raster value is the join key

decision: map carries a not-for-navigation disclaimer
why: ICGC bathymetry metadata says verbatim it may not be used for maritime navigation

decision: everything is CC BY 4.0, derived tiles can be published
why: ICGC reuse page states it plainly and gives a derived-work attribution template

decision: habitat class accuracy is only 40% per class by the spec's own confusion matrix
why: the map must not imply a polygon's class is certain

decision: clipped 2673 isobaths around Tamariu straight off the remote 592MB file in 7 seconds
why: proves the range-read pipeline before I build anything on it; COTA is the attribute, 1m steps from 0 to -59

decision: pulled 310 habitat polygons for the same bbox, 39 of them Posidonia
why: checked the WFS myself rather than trusting the recon summary

decision: print geometry is specified by map scale, not zoom
why: an instructor sets 1:2000 and trusts the scale bar; zoom is derived from scale, latitude and dpi

decision: textures ship at several resolutions, not one
why: user wants 512 for phones and full 2048 for a powerful machine or a print run

decision: MIT licence on the repo
why: user's call

decision: everything vector where it can be; textures are raster patterns masked by vector polygons
why: user asked for vector layers; MapLibre fill-pattern is exactly a raster fill clipped to a vector polygon, so both hold

decision: offline support is a hard requirement, not a nicety
why: divers open this on a boat with no signal

decision: GitHub Pages, static, custom domain divemap.mauri.app
why: free hosting, no server; rules out any runtime tile service

decision: print framing is a draggable crop overlay over the live map
why: user frames each sheet by hand and may print an area with no dive site in it

decision: disclaimer wording is scuba orientation, not marine navigation
why: user confirmed the use; ICGC's restriction is about navigation

decision: fanned out four agents on disjoint file scopes
why: DEM tiles, vector tiles, OSM plus coastline, and deploy plus offline share no files; I kept the visual direction and map style

decision: one lookup resolves a seabed code from either published catalogue
why: the live substrate layer returns 30509, 30512 and 30513, which are seagrass classes the substrate spec never defines; a test over a fixture of real codes now fails if that drifts

decision: seabed as painted terrain, not a nautical chart
why: user pinned the Crosshead Dungeondraft world; a pinned direction beats the roll

decision: depth reads as a water column veil over the texture, not a tint under it
why: alpha carries depth, so shallow stays sharp and warm and deep goes blue and recedes, which is what light actually does in water

decision: wrote a style validator instead of eyeballing the JSON
why: a bad expression makes a MapLibre layer vanish silently rather than throw

decision: shipping JXL alongside WebP, but it earns little here
why: measured at matched PSNR it is level with WebP overall and 10% smaller lossless; only Safari decodes it unflagged

decision: map renders: 325 habitat polygons, 639 isobaths, 7 dive sites at Tamariu
why: first time anything was drawn; every earlier claim was about files, not pixels

decision: vite pre-bundling 404s maplibre's tile worker, so nothing ever loaded and nothing errored
why: found by reading the network log, not the console; the worker dies silently and the map still paints its background

decision: concat needs to-string; a number argument makes the whole label evaluate to nothing
why: isobath and depth labels were silently empty

decision: isobath labels need a 90 degree max angle, not the usual 25
why: measured: 25 places zero labels out of 408 candidate contours over Tamariu, 90 places four of five emphasised depths

decision: slackened the depth veil above 30m
why: measured the seabed texture at 71.6 luminance sd alone and 27.8 under the first veil; divers dive 5 to 40m and that band had stopped reading as ground

decision: land went from pale rock to dark, quiet ground
why: land was reading louder than the seabed, which is the entire subject

decision: chose a local vertex-split repair in vector space, not rasterise-and-revectorise
why: route 2 needs a label grid at 2 m over lon 0.16-3.32 lat 40.5-42.5: 160k x 100k = 16e9 cells, 16 GB at one byte per label before any working copy, against 24 GB free on this machine

decision: route 2, rasterise and re-vectorise, at the source quantum rather than finer
why: a tiling face fan exists at 653 of 96918 candidate vertices, so the shared-edge invariant route 1 wants to keep does not exist in this input; all 1243451 source vertices sit exactly on the 1e-4 deg grid, so that grid is lossless

decision: repartition_polygons.py runs end to end on a 790 feature window
why: clean output: 0 invalid polygons against 672 in the raw, sum of areas equals the union exactly so zero overlap, coverage lost 0.591% and gained 1.220%, 18320 of 18355 pinched corners opened
